reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - GD2 expression was detected in 6/12 evaluable patients (50% positive), confirming the drug reached its intended target. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Clear evidence of downstream biological activity - multiple biomarkers showed expected changes including CRP increase (9-11 mg/dL), lymphocyte dynamics (initial drop to ~225 then rebound to ~4400), soluble IL-2 receptor alpha increase (~1260 to 11000-14000 ng/ml), and anti-idiotypic antibody development. These changes are consistent with immune activation via the GD2-targeted IL-2 delivery mechanism. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Both primary endpoints were met with substantial effect sizes - median RFS of 5.73 months and median OS of 61.57 months in this single-arm study of resectable recurrent stage III/IV melanoma patients. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: The trial showed activity in both GD2-positive and GD2-negative patients (3/11 vs 3/9 in arm A, 3/9 vs 3/9 in arm B), suggesting the mechanism may work regardless of baseline GD2 expression levels. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This is a single-arm study without a control group, which limits definitive efficacy assessment, but the survival outcomes appear favorable for this patient population.

failure_modes.evidence: Single-arm study design without control group limits ability to definitively attribute efficacy to treatment versus natural history or other factors
